skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-google-ads-new-customer-bidding
skill.description: Set up Google Ads bidding for first paid WooCommerce orders with Product Metrics. Check tracking and order classification, then choose a revenue or profit conversion goal in Google Ads.
skill.summary: Verify first-order conversions and choose a new customer bidding goal for WooCommerce in Google Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The reconnaissance alerts describe store setup and conversion checks, and Markdown backticks do not execute code by themselves. The unpinned installer and authenticated remote MCP execution warrant controls on software provenance and action scope. The workflow also needs clearer approval for order data and tighter rules for credentials and remote guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and skill source revision. Present the sources for approval before running a separate install step.

remediation.issue: Broad action scope on the authenticated MCP connection
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist the status, order and conversion operations this skill needs. Use read-only permissions for checks and require user approval before any write.

remediation.issue: External order import and tracking setup lack a distinct approval step
remediation.suggestion: Before import, confirm the data categories, history range, destination and applicable consent settings. Make other ad channels and Customer Match separate opt-ins.

remediation.issue: Order reads rely on discovered account identifiers
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the workspace, store and Ads account before retrieving orders. Limit the sample and return aggregate classifications unless the user needs individual records.

remediation.issue: Unrelated connector rules permit credential collection
remediation.suggestion: Remove the credential exceptions from this workflow. Keep all secrets in the provider's sign-in or plugin interface and keep them out of tool arguments.

remediation.issue: Remote documentation can change after review
remediation.suggestion: Use the bundled references or a pinned revision. Treat live pages as reference data and do not let them authorize new actions.

semantic_findings.title: Order import before explicit data scope approval
semantic_findings.description: The setup can run without a request naming Product Metrics. The WooCommerce guide queues an initial order import before its consent setup step. The Google Ads setup also creates eight conversion actions, beyond the first-order goal.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guides show the import order and broader conversion setup. They require operator clicks but do not ask the operator to approve the data scope separately.

semantic_findings.title: Order reads without explicit store confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow takes company and storefront identifiers from earlier results without requiring the operator to confirm the store. Its classification checks can retrieve order-level margin even when only customer classifications are requested.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The order tools accept scope identifiers, but the text does not require the user to verify the selected scope or minimize the returned fields.

semantic_findings.title: Credential exceptions outside the bidding workflow
semantic_findings.description: The general rules allow the agent to obtain unrelated connector secrets from the user and pass them to a command. That could expose them to tool logging or local process inspection despite the instruction not to repeat them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception names credentials for other integrations, while the WooCommerce setup explicitly keeps its token out of chat. The text does not specify secure secret input.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable documentation can replace bundled steps
semantic_findings.description: When local references are missing, the skill directs the agent to treat current vendor Markdown as equivalent workflow instructions. A later edit could change data or permission requests without marketplace review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback uses live documentation paths with no revision or integrity check. No evidence of malicious content was found in the bundled pages.

content.user_title: Set up Google Ads bidding for new WooCommerce customers
content.value_statement: A standard purchase goal does not distinguish first orders from repeat purchases. Use Product Metrics to check first-order signals and choose a Google Ads goal for new customer bidding.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status and identify which store or Google Ads steps remain.
Check whether recent WooCommerce orders are classified as new, returning or unknown.
Guide the merchant through consent setup and verify that a paid test order reaches Product Metrics.
Compare first-order revenue and profit goals and explain how target ROAS applies to each.
Read back the primary or secondary status of Google Ads conversion actions after the user changes them.
limitations: Requires the Product Metrics Pro workspace, WooCommerce plugin, and a Google Ads account linked to Merchant Center.
The user completes WordPress and Google Ads steps, including the switch to a primary bidding goal.
Profit conversions require complete cost data and active additional costs. Conversion delivery also depends on consent.
Classification depends on WooCommerce paid orders and matching customer accounts or guest billing emails. Some orders remain unknown.

use_cases.title: Check readiness for first-order tracking
use_cases.description: Find which store connection, consent and test-order steps remain before asking Google Ads to bid on first orders.

use_cases.title: Pilot a goal in one campaign
use_cases.description: Choose first-order revenue or profit for one campaign while leaving other campaigns on their current goals.

use_cases.title: Investigate missing conversion signals
use_cases.description: Review paid statuses, unknown classifications, consent and cost coverage to explain gaps between orders and reported conversions.

prompt_templates.title: Check the prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: You are new to first-order bidding.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my approved WooCommerce store and Google Ads account are ready for Product Metrics first-order tracking. List the missing steps without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a recent order sample
prompt_templates.scenario: Your store is connected and you need to check classification.
prompt_templates.prompt: For the store I confirm, group the last 20 paid orders into new, returning and unknown. Report counts without names or emails. Flag any paid-status settings that need review.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an initial bidding goal
prompt_templates.scenario: Tracking is active and you want to test one campaign.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare first-order revenue and profit for my test campaign. Explain the cost requirements and how to set a campaign-specific goal. Do not change the account.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a campaign after the switch
prompt_templates.scenario: You changed a campaign goal in Google Ads and need to verify it.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read back the conversion action status for the property I confirm. Compare it with my intended goal and flag duplicate primary purchase actions. List any campaign settings I should verify in Google Ads.

output_examples.input: Is our confirmed store ready for new customer bidding?
output: The store and Google Ads account are connected.
Live order delivery is still unverified. Use an authorized paid test order to verify delivery before changing the campaign goal.

output_examples.input: What did the last 20 paid orders show?
output: Of 20 paid orders, 8 were new, 10 were returning, and 2 were unknown.
Review the paid status filters and order history before using this sample to assess the first-order conversion signal.
The summary excludes customer names and email addresses.

output_examples.input: Should we use first-order revenue or profit in our pilot?
output: Use first-order revenue for the pilot because product costs are missing from some orders.
Choose Product Metrics - New Customer as the goal for the pilot campaign. Leave the other campaigns on their current goals.
Share confirmation after the change so the conversion action status can be checked.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace, store and Ads account before granting access. Review the order import scope and consent settings before starting the import.
Verify a paid test order and check recent buyer classifications before changing what the campaign bids on.
Pilot one campaign and use one purchase action for bidding. Confirm cost coverage before choosing profit.
anti_patterns: Do not paste setup tokens or account credentials into chat.
Do not treat pending, failed or cancelled orders as paid for first-order classification.
Do not make both revenue and profit primary for the same campaign or switch all campaigns before validating one.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. This workflow uses a Product Metrics Pro workspace, the WooCommerce plugin and a connected Google Ads account.

faq.question: How does the plugin recognize guest customers?
faq.answer: It uses billing email to look for earlier paid WooCommerce orders. A guest with an earlier paid order under the same email counts as returning.

faq.question: Does the skill switch my bidding goal?
faq.answer: No. You choose the goal in Google Ads. The skill can read back the conversion action status after you make the change.

faq.question: What happens if order costs are missing?
faq.answer: An order with missing costs can send revenue but not profit. Check cost coverage before choosing the profit goal.

faq.question: What does a 100% target ROAS mean for first-order profit?
faq.answer: It targets first-order profit equal to ad spend. It does not guarantee that the campaign will achieve that return.

faq.question: What happens when a first order is refunded?
faq.answer: Product Metrics adjusts the Google Ads conversion when the WooCommerce order is refunded or cancelled.
